title: Remove global locks from routing plumbing and modernize fallback contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current smart routing plumbing uses a small set of coarse-grained global mutexes that protect the policy engine, region affinity maps, and fallback registries. Under high QPS (bursty chat workloads) these locks cause tail-latency spikes and create hotspots during rolling deployments. Impact is amplified for Dedicated customers with many concurrent streams.

Investigation summary: Observed lock contention in production traces (trace IDs available in monitor links). Microbenchmarks show p99 request latency increases by ~2.3x when contended. Root causes: (1) single policy registry mutated on route updates, (2) fallback evaluation path requires synchronized mutation of a shared priority queue, (3) regional routing map is rebuilt under a global lock during cluster topology changes.

Goal: Remove or dramatically reduce global locking in the routing stack; implement lock-sharded or lock-free alternatives where feasible; define a smaller, well-documented fallback contract (pure evaluator interface + immutable policy snapshots) to avoid synchronized mutations on hot paths. This ticket covers design, prototype refactor, tests, and controlled rollout to canary region.

Work items: design immutable policy snapshot representation; replace global policy registry with epoched atomic pointer + copy-on-write updates; shard region affinity maps by region id and move topology rebuilds to background reconciler; change fallback registry to store references to stateless evaluators and make dynamic scoring a read-only operation on the hot path; add contention metrics and lock-hold histograms to telemetry.

Notes on tradeoffs: Copy-on-write snapshot reduces write latency and lock contention at the cost of more memory churn during high churn updates. Sharding increases code complexity and requires careful testing around cross-shard routing rules. We prefer correctness and tail latency over saving a small amount of memory for now.
acceptance_criteria: p99 tail latency attributable to routing lock contention reduced by at least 40% in synthetic stress tests compared to baseline
no global mutex held on the hot path for request evaluation in production build (verified by audit and eBPF traces)
policy updates are atomic from the request evaluator's perspective (test harness validates snapshot semantics)
fallback evaluators are invoked without any synchronized mutations on hot path and are covered by unit + integration tests
canary rollout (us-west-2) shows no increase in error rate or CPU across service replicas for 48h under representative load
benchmarks and memory profiles included in PR description

implementation_notes: Use an atomic pointer (or equivalent in service language) to publish immutable PolicyBundle structs. Writers build new bundles and atomically swap.
Shard RegionAffinityMap by region_id mod N_SHARDS. Choose N_SHARDS=8 as starting point; expose an env var to tune in canary.
FallbackEvaluator interface must be pure-function style: Evaluate(readonlyContext) -> FallbackDecision. Move any metrics aggregation off hot path to async reporters.
Add eBPF-based lock hold tracing in the staging cluster to validate no long-held mutexes remain.
Update SDK compatibility matrix if API surface changes (none expected for callers, only internal).
